instruction: You are a strategic corporate innovation advisor. Analyse the company profile and survey responses, then respond ONLY with a valid JSON object containing maturity_score, opportunities, next_steps, and key_weaknesses.

answers.companyDescription: Municipal government administration serving a population of 250,000 residents with services spanning urban planning, waste management, social services, and cultural programming. The company is heavily invested in deploying IoT infrastructure to optimize resource allocation across its service portfolio. While operational scale is large, the central decision-making structure remains lean, relying on expert technical advice for policy implementation.
answers.pastInitiatives: We have a mature innovation program with a dedicated R&D lab of 12 engineers, an annual innovation budget equivalent to 5% of revenue, and a structured stage-gate process for evaluating and funding new initiatives. In the past 3 years we have launched 4 new product lines that now contribute 18% of total revenue, including an AI-powered recommendation engine that has become our fastest-growing SKU.
answers.strategicGoals: The board has challenged us to improve EBITDA margins by 500 basis points within 3 years. This requires a disciplined, data-driven approach to identifying cost drivers and process bottlenecks. We are open to technology investment if it demonstrably reduces unit costs or eliminates manual touchpoints, but every project must have a clear ROI timeline of under 12 months.
answers.additionalContext: We completed a merger with a similarly-sized competitor 4 months ago and are in the middle of integrating teams, systems, and processes. The combined organization has significant duplication—two CRMs, two HR systems, overlapping product lines. There is a unique window to redesign processes from scratch rather than patching legacy approaches, but cultural integration is fragile and change fatigue is real.
answers.teamSize: We have a small technology team of 4-6 people including developers, a part-time DevOps engineer, and a product manager who also handles project management. The team is fully allocated to maintaining current products and handling integration requests from key clients. Innovation work is done in the margins — there is no formally ring-fenced innovation time or budget.

opportunities.title: AI-Driven Policy Optimization Engine (Radical)
opportunities.rationale: Leverage the existing data infrastructure and AI expertise to transition from optimizing current processes to radically re-engineering decision pathways. This could allow for automated, real-time policy adjustments based on live sensor data (e.g., traffic flow, energy consumption) rather than static rules.

first_actions: Establish a cross-functional task force dedicated solely to identifying the top three most manual/repetitive decision points in waste management and traffic signaling.
resources_needed: Allocation of 2 full-time Data Scientists focused on predictive modeling.
Pilot budget for sandbox testing new ML algorithms (approx. $50k).
execution_plan.success_metric: Reduction in manual operational decision time by 40% within 18 months.
milestones: Q3: Pilot deployment of the optimization engine on a single waste management zone.

opportunities.title: Hyper-Automation of Citizen Services Portal (Efficiency)
opportunities.rationale: Implement Robotic Process Automation (RPA) and advanced chatbots to handle high-volume, standardized inquiries related to permits and service requests. This addresses immediate time constraints by offloading routine tasks from the small team.

first_actions: Inventory all top 10 repetitive citizen service tickets and map current workflow.
resources_needed: Training time for existing product management staff.
execution_plan.success_metric: 25% reduction in average ticket resolution time; 10-person team reallocation of 1 FTE.
milestones: Q4: Implementation of chatbot and RPA on the top five service workflows.

next_steps.action: Conduct a comprehensive audit of system duplication and define an integration roadmap for merging CRM/HR systems.
Form a dedicated 'Efficiency Squad' to prioritize the radical policy optimization project over feature development in Q1.

key_weaknesses: Severe talent scarcity within the core technology team hindering the pace of innovation.
Fragile cultural integration following the recent merger leading to change fatigue and siloed operations.
Lack of formal, protected time/budget for strategic innovation work, forcing tech teams into reactive mode.
High operational drag due to significant system duplication that prevents true process re-engineering.
